tips.title: Selecting the Right Paint for Your Project
tips.text: Choose between Vallejo Acrylic, Vallejo Model Air, or Tamiya Acrylics for their ease of use, vibrant colors, and fast drying times. For enamel or lacquer finishes, use AMMO by Mig Jimenez Acrylic Paints or Humbrol Enamels, but expect slower drying times and more solvents. Vallejo Metal Color or Alclad II Aerosols provide excellent metal finishes. Always thin paints with their respective thinners (e.g., Vallejo Airbrush Thinner) for optimal flow.

tips.title: Choosing the Right Sandpaper Grits for Each Stage
tips.text: For initial sanding after filling, use 120-150 grit sandpaper or sanding sticks to remove excess filler and prepare the surface. For smoothing and preparing for paint, switch to 240-320 grit, then finish with 400-600 grit for a smooth surface. For fine touch-ups, use 800-1000 grit wet or dry sandpaper. Always wet-sand with water or appropriate lubricant to prevent clogging and achieve the best results.

tips.title: Filling Gaps: Tamiya vs Vallejo Putty
tips.text: For small gaps and scratches, use Tamiya Putty, which dries fast and can be sanded in 30 minutes. For larger gaps or panel lines, Vallejo Plastic Putty offers better coverage and can be applied thicker. Both can be used with Vallejo Retarder Medium to extend drying times. To make your own gap filler, mix super glue with baking soda, apply with a fine brush, let dry, and sand smooth. Always test on spare parts first.

tips.title: Photo-Etch vs Resin Detail Parts
tips.text: Photo-etch (PE) from Eduard, ICM, or other brands offers thin, highly detailed parts, perfect for replacing kit details. However, PE requires bending, cutting, and careful handling. Resin detail sets (e.g., Lion Roar, Cyber-Hobby) offer pre-shaped, high-quality parts but can be more expensive. Consider PE for simple replacement details, and resin for complex shapes or when quality is paramount.

tips.title: Decal Setting Solutions: Micro Set/Sol vs Mr. Mark Softer
tips.text: For standard decals, use Micro Set (soaking solution) followed by Micro Sol (setting solution) to help decals conform and minimize silvering. For difficult-to-place or complex decals, use Mr. Mark Softer, which penetrates better and helps decals lie flat. Apply Micro Set or Mr. Mark Softer with a fine brush, let soak for 10-20 seconds, then carefully apply Micro Sol to set the decal. Always test on spare decals first.
